```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(purrr)
library(readr)
library(tidyr)
```

## Problem 1

I represented birthdays using the numbers 1 through 365. Then I sampled with
replacement so that more than one person could be born on the same day.

```{r}
set.seed(8105)

shared_birthday = function(group_size) {
  birthdays = sample(1:365, size = group_size, replace = TRUE)
  any(duplicated(birthdays))
}

birthday_sim =
  expand_grid(
    group_size = 2:50,
    iter = 1:10000
  ) |>
  mutate(
    shared = map(group_size, shared_birthday)
  ) |>
  unnest(shared)
```

Each row represents one simulated group. I averaged the TRUE/FALSE results
within each group size to estimate the probability of a shared birthday.

```{r prob}
birthday_prob =
  birthday_sim |>
  group_by(group_size) |>
  summarize(probability = mean(shared))
```

```{r plot, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
birthday_prob |>
  ggplot(aes(x = group_size, y = probability)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  labs(
    title = "How likely is a shared birthday?",
    x = "Number of people",
    y = "Estimated probability"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

With just 23 people, the chance of a shared birthday was already about 52%.
It reached about 97% with 50 people. As the group gets larger, there are
more pairs of people who could share a birthday.

## Problem 2

Each CSV file contains eight weekly observations for one participant.
I used the filename to identify the study arm and participant ID.

```{r}
participant_files =
  tibble(
    file_name = list.files("data", pattern = "[.]csv$"),
    path = file.path("data", file_name)
  ) |>
  mutate(data = map(path, read_csv, show_col_types = FALSE))
```

```{r}
longitudinal_data =
  participant_files |>
  mutate(file_name = stringr::str_remove(file_name, "[.]csv$")) |>
  separate(file_name, into = c("arm", "subject_id"), sep = "_") |>
  mutate(arm = recode(arm, con = "Control", exp = "Experimental")) |>
  select(-path) |>
  unnest(data) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("week_"),
    names_to = "week",
    names_prefix = "week_",
    values_to = "observation"
  ) |>
  mutate(week = as.integer(week))

longitudinal_data
```

```{r spaghetti-plot, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.5}
longitudinal_data |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = week, y = observation,
    group = interaction(arm, subject_id), color = arm
  )) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:8) +
  labs(
    title = "Weekly observations by study arm",
    x = "Week",
    y = "Observation",
    color = "Study arm"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

The two groups overlap early in the study. Most experimental participants
have higher observations in the later weeks than at the start. The control
participants' observations fluctuate over time, with no consistent increase.
